FIRS’s rollout slows or changes?
What are CAC, payback period, sales-cycle length and conversion rates by direct sales, accountants and partner channels?
How many invoices are validated automatically, how many are rejected or manually reviewed, and what error, filing and support rates have you seen?
What controls prevent incorrect filings, who bears liability for errors, and have there been material customer incidents or penalties?
Who are the closest alternatives—accountants, ERP vendors, tax firms and competing software—and why do customers switch or stay?
Show the cash position, monthly burn bridge, runway under current and planned burn, and the assumptions behind Q3 2028 break-even.
Why is the raise $1.8m, how will each use-of-funds category translate into customers or revenue, and what milestones should be reached before the next round?
What is the CTO’s relevant operating history, how is engineering organised, and can the team support integrations, security, data protection and FIRS changes at scale?

My view is to treat Ledgerline as a potentially relevant seed-stage fit for your stated interest in African fintech and B2B software, with reported traction strong enough to justify structured diligence, not yet enough to resolve the key questions. The highest-value next step is a founder call focused on revenue quality, retention cohorts, customer concentration, compliance reliability and the burn-to-break-even plan. The public search added no reliable corroboration of Ledgerline’s company-specific traction or team claims; one apparent match was explicitly labelled an illustrative placeholder, so I have not used it as evidence.
